newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Coffee poised to push higher, set new high.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Coffee poised to push higher, set new high.

text.p: JULY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Robusta coffee futures are likely to continue this week's rally as the benchmark July contract prepares to challenge its life-high of $1,820 a tonne, technical analysts said on Friday.
Traders called London to open $25 higher than Thursday's close as speculative buying in New York boosted July arabicas by 5.50 cents/lb on the day to 216.90 after an intraday high of 219.50.
The higher call would immediately bring July robustas to $1,800, just $20 away from the contract high scored on March 11. It would be an 11-month high on a second-month continuation basis.
Technically, the outlook improved significantly when July filled a gap between $1,692 and $1,730 earlier in the week.
"From the technical point of view, the fact that that gap was filled removed an obstacle," said Adrian Haylor, a technical analyst at Sucden. "It looks like we will be breaking through $1,800."
"This leaves the whole technical outlook looking much better and sets up a test of the $1,820 high," he said.
The position was well supported at $1,700, and slightly above, while short-term moving averages were gathered in a broad band between $1,630 and $1,665.
In fundamental news, portworkers at south Brazil's key port of Santos are set to return to work at 1000 GMT on Friday after staging a 24-hour protest over a delay in receiving their April salary.
But a decision on whether to stage a full strike will depend on the outcome of talks to be held later between union officials and port authority representatives.
The Santos strike, which only affected public terminals, sparked enough buying of July arabicas on Thursday to trigger technical buy stops above 213.50.
